newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin op, US rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease on Yeltsin op, US rate fears.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased on Tuesday on uncertainty about President Boris Yeltsin's health and fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates later today, dealers said.
A team of doctors will meet Yeltsin at around noon (0800 GMT) on Wednesday and discuss a possible date for his planned heart operation.

Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon expected to lead Yeltsin's planned heart operation, said on Tuesday there was no chance of the surgery being cancelled. He had previously said the operation could be delayed for up to two months or maybe not held at all.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee is meeting today to see if and by how much the U.S. raises interest rates. Dealers were speculating previously on a rise of 25 basis points.

"Some major London operators were earlier selling big packages, mainly in the fourth and fifth tranches. When it ended, prices firmed a little on apparently local buying," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.
A London bank dealer said a likely rise in U.S. interest rates seemed another depressing factor, no less important than medical news from the Kremlin.
"The weaker trend is caused by two reasons, expectations that U.S. rates might go up and uncertainty about Yeltsin's ill health," he said.

But the ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said: "If there is some uncertainty inside Russia, it is the most important thing for this market. If it is calm here, the market starts looking at something else (going on abroad)."
"Nervousness about the heart operation on Yeltsin seemed the main factor for (earlier Western) selling, given its high volumes," he added.
Dealers forecast prices could ease further on Wednesday, with the market awaiting the results of doctors' meeting with Yeltsin.
The London bank dealer said prices could be pressured further by continuing worries about Yeltsin. He added banks could otherwise take profits after the rise over the recent month.
The ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said: "Much will depend on the doctors' meeting but generally people prefer to sell on this kind of news."
